supersaturation deposits ice and undersaturation sublimates it (3 draws)
at saturation phi_t = -M dF/dphi with M > 0, so F decreases (3 draws, phi = 0.3 and 0.7)

relaxation: -(6*eps*gamma*(Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (x, 2)) + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (y, 2)) + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (z, 2))) - 6*gamma*(1 - 2*phi(x, y, z, t))*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*phi(x, y, z, t)/eps)*M(T(x, y, z, t))
driving force: -30*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))**2*(rho_v(x, y, z, t) - rho_vs(T(x, y, z, t)))*alpha(T(x, y, z, t))*phi(x, y, z, t)**2

relaxation: - 3*M*eps*(Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (x, 2)) + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (y, 2)) + Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), (z, 2))) + 3*M/eps*phi(x, y, z, t)*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*(1 - 2*phi(x, y, z, t))
driving force: -alpha/rho_i*phi(x, y, z, t)**2*(1 - phi(x, y, z, t))**2*(rho_v(x, y, z, t) - rho_vs(T(x, y, z, t)))

agent's symbols.name: M(T)
agent's symbols.meaning: Interface mobility. It sets how fast $\phi$ relaxes toward a minimum of $F$, and so how fast curvature (Gibbs–Thomson) moves the interface. A positive kinetic coefficient.

agent's symbols.name: alpha(T)
agent's symbols.meaning: Deposition and sublimation rate coefficient: the rate of change of $\phi$ at the interface per unit vapor excess $\rho_v-\rho_{vs}$. It is related to the Hertz–Knudsen kinetic velocity $\beta$ by $\alpha=\beta/(6\varepsilon\rho_i)$.

agent's symbols.name: beta
agent's symbols.meaning: Kinetic velocity of the Hertz–Knudsen law, $\alpha_s\sqrt{k_B T/(2\pi m_w)}$, where $\alpha_s$ is the sticking coefficient. Used only to interpret $\alpha$.

agent's symbols.name: v
agent's symbols.meaning: Normal speed of a planar front

agent's symbols.name: phi0
agent's symbols.meaning: Equilibrium profile of a flat interface

agent's symbols.name: xi
agent's symbols.meaning: Coordinate normal to a flat interface

agent left out.effect: Nonlinear dependence on supersaturation, for example $\ln(\rho_v/\rho_{vs})$
agent left out.why: Supersaturations in the pores are small, $|\rho_v/\rho_{vs}-1|\ll1$. The dropped terms are of order $(\rho_v/\rho_{vs}-1)^2$.

agent left out.effect: Anisotropy of the ice surface energy and of the attachment kinetics
agent left out.why: $\gamma$ is constant by the work order. Faceting at the pore scale is a secondary effect for the bulk transport of ice.
The interface width $\varepsilon\sim\mu$m is much larger than the thermal length $\sqrt{k_BT/\gamma}\sim0.2$ nm.

agent left out.effect: Regolith grains as a third phase, including wetting by ice
agent left out.why: The work order describes only ice and gas in the pore space. Grains would enter as boundary conditions or as a fixed field.

agent left out.effect: Latent heat and vapor mass exchange
agent left out.why: They couple $\phi$ back to $T$ and $\rho_v$. Those equations are separate tasks; here the fields are given.

agent left out.effect: Elastic stress and mechanical motion of ice
agent left out.why: The ice is treated as rigid and fixed in place. Stresses are small compared with the vapor-driven changes.

agent left out.effect: A thermodynamically consistent link between $M$ and $\alpha$
agent left out.why: I kept them as separate coefficients. Thermodynamic consistency would require $\alpha/M=\rho_i k_BT/(m_w\rho_{vs})$. This changes curvature effects only through the ratio $\varepsilon/$(radius of curvature).
